## SUN → $W_{72}$\: Recovery of the earliest coordinate definitions

**The earliest recovered SUN definitions establish the scalar musical operators and the Fludd–Kepler register boundary. They do not establish a unique native coordinate lift $\widehat R,\widehat L$ into $W_{72}$\.**

However, the October 9 recovered formulation contains a more specific coordinate convention than our recent discussion acknowledged. It gives us a legitimate starting point for deriving angular displacements and exact residuals **without modifying SUN**\.

### 1\. Recovered chronology and authority

| Stage | Recovered definition | Status |
|--------|--------|--------|
| September 10–11 | $R=2/3,\ L=3/4$, musical diamond and octave closure | Confirmed in recovered chronology |
| September 12 | Three ordinary generations, followed by the separately specified Fludd–Kepler boundary | Confirmed in recovered checkpoint |
| Subsequent $W_{72}$ work | $W_{12}\rightarrow W_{36}\rightarrow W_{72}$, with ternary and binary refinement | Recovered carrier construction |
| October 9 | $S=(c,g,p,\tau,\beta,\rho)$, with an exact logarithmic pitch-coordinate convention | Recovered proposed formulation |
| Current investigation | Full native $\widehat R,\widehat L$ actions on all coordinates | **Unresolved** |

The crucial point is that **the original scalar SUN equation predates the recovered $W_{72}$ representation**\. Its ratios cannot retrospectively be treated as evidence that a particular ternary or binary traversal was originally defined.

## 2\. The angular offsets can be derived conditionally

The October 9 formulation used the coordinate convention

$$
\boxed{
\log_2(f/f_*)=g+\frac p{12}+\rho.
}
$$

Here $g$ is an integer register coordinate, $p$ is a twelve-position address, and $\rho$ retains the exact logarithmic displacement not represented by the register and nominal angular position.

Under this convention, the descending scalar SUN operators have exact pitch displacements\:

$$
d_R=\log_2(2/3)\approx-0.584962501,
$$

$$
d_L=\log_2(3/4)\approx-0.415037499.
$$

In semitone units\:

$$
12d_R\approx-7.019550009,
$$

$$
12d_L\approx-4.980449991.
$$

The natural nearest-semitone decomposition is therefore\:

$$
\boxed{\Delta p_R=-7\pmod{12}=5,}
$$

$$
\boxed{\Delta p_L=-5\pmod{12}=7.}
$$

These are **derived under the recovered equal-tempered coordinate convention**, not independently established ancient or original SUN address assignments.

The exact residual changes are\:

$$
\boxed{
\Delta\rho_R
=
\log_2(2/3)+\frac7{12}
\approx-0.0016291674,
}
$$

$$
\boxed{
\Delta\rho_L
=
\log_2(3/4)+\frac5{12}
\approx+0.0016291674.
}
$$

Their cancellation is exact\:

$$
\Delta\rho_R+\Delta\rho_L=0.
$$

And their nominal steps add to one descending octave\:

$$
-7-5=-12.
$$

Thus the recovered scalar closure has a consistent lifted representation\:

$$
\boxed{
(\Delta\text{ nominal semitones},\Delta\rho)
=
(-12,0).
}
$$

This is already a meaningful result: **the ordinary SUN diamond closes exactly in both the nominal octave displacement and the accumulated residual.**

The remaining convention issue is register sign. The logarithmic equation above uses $g$ increasing with frequency, whereas the September 12 Fludd–Kepler grade uses $+1$ for a descending octave. They cannot be silently identified. One can keep the two grades distinct or explicitly convert between them.

## 3\. An earlier $W_{72}$ definition was recovered

The file **`Pasted markdown(20260919-041032).md`** contains explicit coordinate operators, predating the October 9 formulation.

This is the most important recovery.

It defines the *ascending reciprocal* musical operations, not the descending SUN operations\:

$$
R_\uparrow=\frac32,\qquad
L_\uparrow=\frac43.
$$

Their nominal angular actions are

$$
\boxed{
R_\uparrow:p\mapsto p+7\pmod{12},
}
$$

$$
\boxed{
L_\uparrow:p\mapsto p+5\pmod{12}.
}
$$

Their exact residual updates have equal magnitudes and opposite signs.

The source also defines an **axis firewall**\:

- Acoustic operators act on $(g,p,\rho)$\.
- Ternary and binary phase operators act on $(\tau,\beta)$\.
- Refinement maps introduce coordinates without relocating existing addresses.

Most importantly, it gives the checksum

$$
\boxed{
C(R_\uparrow L_\uparrow)
=(1,0,0,0,0).
}
$$

That is the ascending octave convention. It is consistent with

$$
\frac32\cdot\frac43=2.
$$

For the descending SUN operators, the corresponding inverse checksum is

$$
\boxed{
C(R_\downarrow L_\downarrow)
=(-1,0,0,0,0)
}
$$

under that same ascending-positive register convention.

**This resolves three of your four questions within the recovered September 19 $W_{72}$ model.**

| Coordinate | Descending SUN lift under the recovered $W_{72}$ convention |
|--------|--------|
| Angular $p$ | $R:-7,\ L:-5\pmod{12}$ |
| Ternary $\tau$ | Unchanged by $R,L$ |
| Binary $\beta$ | Unchanged by $R,L$ |
| Exact residual $\rho$ | Opposite, cancelling updates |
| Register | Integer carry from the unwrapped angular traversal |

This is stronger than my initial statement that no coordinate definition had been recovered.

### A complete lifted formula

Let

$$
\delta=\log_2(3/2)-\frac7{12}.
$$

Then

$$
\log_2(4/3)-\frac5{12}=-\delta.
$$

For a state

$$
s=(g,p,\tau,\beta,\rho),
$$

using the ascending-positive register convention and $0\le p<12$, the descending lifts are\:

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\widehat R_\downarrow(s)
&=
\left(
g+\left\lfloor\frac{p-7}{12}\right\rfloor,\
(p-7)\bmod12,\
\tau,\beta,\
\rho-\delta
\right),\\[4pt]
\widehat L_\downarrow(s)
&=
\left(
g+\left\lfloor\frac{p-5}{12}\right\rfloor,\
(p-5)\bmod12,\
\tau,\beta,\
\rho+\delta
\right).
\end{aligned}
}
$$

These formulas are a derived explicit realization of the recovered September 19 conventions.

Their composition gives

$$
\boxed{
\widehat R_\downarrow
\widehat L_\downarrow(s)
=
(g-1,p,\tau,\beta,\rho).
}
$$

The order is immaterial for these exact translations.

They preserve the scalar identity

$$
\frac23\cdot\frac34=\frac12
$$

and preserve the phase coordinates without inventing an interaction.

## 4\. The Fludd–Kepler threshold is still a separate unresolved binding

The September 12 checkpoint specifies the boundary path

$$
15\longrightarrow16\longrightarrow7.5,
$$

with its local return and register displacement.

But **I have not recovered a primary definition proving that this boundary triggers precisely when $p=11\rightarrow0$**\.

The September 19 angular lift supplies ordinary register carry whenever a nominal angular step crosses the coordinate seam. That is a bookkeeping operation.

The Fludd–Kepler boundary is a separately specified musical event. Its trigger cannot be identified with every ordinary coordinate seam crossing without an additional rule.

Thus the two questions remain distinct\:

$$
\text{When does a coordinate representation carry register?}
$$

versus

$$
\text{When does SUN invoke the special Fludd–Kepler boundary?}
$$

The first is resolved by the floor terms above. The second remains **UNRESOLVED** as a $W_{72}$ trigger.

## 5\. What this means for the current investigation

We now have an earlier, source-independent mathematical candidate for the operation-preserving lift\:

$$
\boxed{
\widehat R_\downarrow,\widehat L_\downarrow
\text{ preserve }\tau,\beta
\text{ and update }g,p,\rho\text{ exactly.}
}
$$

The recovered September 19 model also gives a clear reason not to identify the binary coordinate with physical divider memory by default: its native binary action $B$ is a separate phase operation, not part of $R$ or $L$\.

The remaining work is therefore narrower than previously stated\:

1. Verify the complete September 19 operator definitions and their provenance against the frozen SUN baseline.
2. Reconcile ascending-positive $g$ with the Fludd–Kepler descending-positive grade.
3. Recover the actual boundary-trigger definition, if one exists.
4. Determine whether the refinement operators $E_3,E_2$ and phase operators $T,B$ have any independently established coupling to musical path admissibility.

**The earliest recovered $W_{72}$ model already answers $\Delta p,\Delta\tau,\Delta\beta$\. It does not establish a state-dependent Fludd–Kepler trigger.**

That is the appropriate checkpoint: recover and verify the September 19 lift before adding anything to the kernel, and keep the Exodus anomaly hunt frozen.
